problemSignature.symptom: The AI command layer used older command names that did not align with the canonical BoardForge CLI verbs.

rootCause: Codex/AI adapters had their own command vocabulary while the product CLI was moving toward create, validate, route, cleanup, export, report, and replay. That could make web, KiCad, and AI surfaces diverge.
fixSummary: Normalize AI command aliases into canonical product commands, map each command to a guarded BoardForge CLI verb and engine job preview, and document the model-agnostic contract.

testsAdded: AI command layer normalizes aliases and maps to canonical CLI verbs

conditions: Use for Codex, web agent, KiCad plugin, or other AI assistant adapters
Use dry-run planning by default before executing local board actions
Use canonical CLI verbs as the shared execution boundary

recipe: Normalize legacy adapter commands into canonical BoardForge commands.
Reject protected project paths before planning execution.
Attach CLI command line and engine job preview to accepted AI commands.
Keep adapters model-agnostic: no Codex-only assumptions in the engine contract.
safetyRules: Do not bypass protected path guards from AI commands.
Do not execute by default; dry-run planning remains the safe default.
Do not let aliases create hidden behavior that differs from canonical CLI verbs.

after.aiCommands: canonical commands with compatibility aliases and CLI mapping
